name: Shallum
overview: Shallum was a male member of the tribe of Judah, identified uniquely as the son of Shaul and grandson of Simeon. His lineage is briefly noted in 1 Chronicles 4:25, situating him within the genealogical records of Israel. Beyond this, there are no additional personal details or notes recorded about him in Scripture.
namesAndTitles: The name Shallum means 'peace, well-being, prosperity' in Hebrew. It is a proper name and was not given directly by God. This meaning reflects a positive and hopeful attribute, although the biblical text does not elaborate on how this meaning related to his life or character.
familyAndRelationships: Shallum is explicitly identified as the son of Shaul, and it is inferred that Mibsam is his father, indicating a lineage within the tribe of Judah. These relationships are documented in 1 Chronicles 4:25. Scripture does not provide further information about his family beyond these connections.
scriptureSignificance: Shallum's significance lies primarily in his place within the genealogical record of Judah, which serves to preserve the heritage and tribal history of Israel. His mention contributes to the biblical emphasis on lineage and God's providential care in maintaining the descendants of His chosen people. Although not a prominent figure in narrative events, his inclusion underscores the faithfulness of God in preserving His covenant people through generations.
